subject: Post-demo: Clarify data roles, subprocessors, and breach-notice expectations
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Riley Barnes <riley@medsync.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo: Clarify data roles, subprocessors, and breach-notice expectations

Hi Riley — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so our legal/ops teams can prepare a tailored DPA and subprocessor inventory for you. TL;DR: attaching a draft DPA and a short SOC 2 summary to accelerate the review.

Recap of asks from your side:
- Confirm whether MedSync will be acting as controller for patient/clinical data (you sign primary consent/notice) and Redwood would be the processor for inference/serving.
- Clarify required data residency (you mentioned US-East and an EU region for pilot customers).
- Expected breach-notice timeline (you said internal legal prefers a 24h preliminary notification; want to confirm).
- Subprocessor transparency: you asked for an inventory + ability to object to new subprocessors.
- Types of PII/PHI in scope (names, MRN, DOB, limited clinical notes vs. raw DICOM).

Questions for you (please answer inline if easiest):
1) Controller vs. processor: confirm MedSync intends to be controller for the pilot (yes/no).
2) Residency: which region(s) must we guarantee for inference/log retention for the pilot?
3) Breach notify: is 24 hours a hard requirement or an ideal target? If hard, any flexibility around preliminary vs. final investigation windows?
4) Subprocessors: do you require prior approval for all subprocessors, or an objection window (e.g., 10 business days) after we share an inventory?

Next steps from Redwood if we get answers:
- Share a redlined DPA (attached) with controller/processor mapping filled in.
- Provide a subprocessor list and SOC2 summary (attached).
- Schedule a 30-min legal alignment call with your legal lead (cc'ing Ben).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf (high-level mapping and notify windows), SOC2-Summary-2027.pdf (scope + controls).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate times for a quick legal alignment call once you confirm who from your team should join.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | https://www.redwoodinference.com

From: Riley Barnes <riley@medsync.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amira Khan <amira.k@medsync.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jan 2028 18:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarify data roles, subprocessors, and breach-notice expectations

Tessa — appreciate the write-up and the DPA draft. Quick answers inline below. Forwarding to Amira (legal) who will take the contract review lead.

1) Controller vs. processor: MedSync will be controller for patient data and any clinical records we collect; we expect Redwood to be a processor for inference and any hosted assets.

2) Residency: For the pilot, US-East is required; for EU beta customers we’ll need an EU-hosted option (likely Ireland). We’ll confirm the list of pilot customers separately.

3) Breach notify: Our legal team prefers a preliminary notification within 24 hours of identifying a potential incident that materially affects patient data, and a full report within 72 hours. If you can provide a short preliminary note sooner for critical events that’s ideal.

4) Subprocessors: we generally operate under an objection model — provide a list and we’ll review. We do reserve the right to object to specific subprocessors for regulated data. A 10 business-day review window works for us.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood will provide audit logs for per-tenant request traces and how long those logs are retained by default? We’ll need that to map to our retention policy.

Thanks — Amira will propose a time for a legal sync.

—Riley
Head of Partnerships, MedSync

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jan 2028 20:03:00 -0500
Subject: FW: Post-demo: Clarify data roles, subprocessors, and breach-notice expectations

Forwarding Riley's answers — a few internal notes / proposal for the legal call:

- Controller/Processor: Riley confirmed MedSync = controller, Redwood = processor. That matches our standard commercial posture; legal will need to confirm exact language in the DPA.
- Residency: US-East required for pilot; EU region (Ireland) for EU customers. We should pre-populate the DPA with region options and our standard region-fallthrough (run in requested region where available, fallback to nearest region with notice).
- Breach notify: their ask = prelim in 24h, full report 72h. Our usual commitment is to make good-faith preliminary notifications as soon as we have credible evidence and deliver a root-cause + mitigation plan within 72h. We need Ben to confirm if we can commit to 24h preliminary notification for controller-level PII events or whether we say "as soon as practicable (target 24h)".
- Subprocesssors: 10-business-day objection window is reasonable. We should prepare a current subprocessor spreadsheet to send prior to the call.
- Logs: they want per-tenant request traces + retention period. Our default is 90 days of request logs; we can propose 90 days with an option for extended retention at cost. Ben — can you confirm if 90 days is ok to offer and whether we can scope a paid option for 12 months?

Action items:
- Ben: review DPA draft and advise on 24h language + log retention concession (Ben to join legal call).
- Tessa: schedule a 30-min call with Amira + Riley + Ben next week. Include subprocessor inventory and SOC2 summary in calendar invite.

Connor
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Riley Barnes <riley@medsync.ai>, Amira Khan <amira.k@medsync.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jan 2028 10:58:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarify data roles, subprocessors, and breach-notice expectations

Riley / Amira — thanks for the quick responses and for looping Amira in. Ben and Connor both confirmed internally; below is Redwood's proposed position so legal can triage before the sync.

Proposed Redwood position (to put on the table ahead of the call):
- Roles: Redwood will act as processor for the inference service and any transient storage we use to fulfill requests. We are happy to sign a DPA that lists MedSync as controller and Redwood as processor.
- Breach notification: Redwood commits to immediate operational alerts to customers on any detection we reasonably consider material. We propose the following contractual timeline: preliminary notification within 24–48 hours where we have initial evidence (target: 24h), and a substantive incident report + remediation plan within 72 hours of initial detection. If there are dependencies on third-party subprocessors that extend investigation time, we will communicate status updates during the 72h window.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a complete current subprocessor inventory prior to the call and agrees to an objection window of 10 business days for MedSync. For any future additions we will provide notice and an objection window as well.
- Logs & retention: Standard request-level audit logs (per-tenant) are retained for 90 days by default. We can offer extended retention (up to 12 months) as a paid add-on; we’ll include that option in the DPA.
- Residency: We will guarantee US-East for the pilot; EU-hosted option (Ireland) available for EU customers. Region-specific routing will be written into the DPA.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll send an updated DPA with the controller/processor mapping and the proposed timelines above (DocuSign envelope linked).
2) Ben and Amira sync — propose a 30-min slot: Thu 1/26 11:00AM ET or Fri 1/27 9:00AM ET. Please confirm preferred time and attendees.
3) I’ll attach the current subprocessor spreadsheet to the meeting invite (no binaries in the thread; will share Drive link).

Links / attachments we’re sharing now:
- DPA draft (DocuSign envelope): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/envelope/EID-9f7a2bd
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/MS-2028-0042
- SOC2 summary (attached to the calendar invite).

If that all looks good, I’ll schedule the legal alignment call and drop the subprocessor inventory into a shared drive for review.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
